ref_extractions.title: Spatiotemporal Analysis of Brain Functional Connectivity
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: Paper describes K-means clustering of PLV connectivity graphs during picture naming with 6 subjects using identical 256-channel EGI EEG system at 1kHz from the conneXion study. However, uses only 6 subjects (vs 23 in dataset) and does not explicitly reference openneuro_ds003420, suggesting it may predate the public dataset release.
ref_extractions.epoch_params: tmin=-0.2s baseline, connectivity computed from stimulus onset
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Methodology directly matches dataset paradigm but sample size discrepancy (6 vs 23) and no explicit dataset reference; likely uses data from same study/conneXion project.

ref_extractions.title: The dynamic functional core network of the human brain at rest
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper studies resting-state functional networks in 20 subjects during task-free paradigm, not task-related activity. While it uses dense EEG and similar source connectivity methods, it does not use the visual naming/spelling dataset (openneuro_ds003420) which involves active task performance.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Different paradigm (resting-state vs picture naming); no mention of naming/spelling tasks from conneXion project.

ref_extractions.title: SimiNet: a Novel Method for Quantifying Brain Network Similarity
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: Paper applies SimiNet algorithm to real brain networks during picture naming comparing animals vs tools categories. Methodology section indicates use of dense-EEG during visual recognition task but does not explicitly cite openneuro_ds003420; likely uses data from same conneXion study or similar paradigm.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Two-category visual object recognition task using dense-EEG; likely from same research group paradigm but explicit dataset reference missing.

ref_extractions.title: An EEG-based methodology for the estimation of functional brain connectivity networks: Application to the analysis of newborn EEG seizure
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper focuses on newborn EEG seizure detection using 79 infant datasets from Helsinki University Hospital. Completely different clinical domain and patient population from the adult visual naming dataset (openneuro_ds003420).
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Neonatal seizure EEG dataset; no relationship to adult picture naming paradigm.

ref_extractions.title: Dynamic reorganization of functional brain networks during picture naming
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This is the primary methodological paper for the dataset paradigm. Explicitly describes the conneXion study with 21 subjects performing picture naming using 256-channel dense EEG at 1kHz, identifying 6 Brain Network States (BNSs) through gamma-band PLV clustering. The dataset (openneuro_ds003420) is the public release of this data.
ref_extractions.epoch_params: tmin=-0.2s, tmax=0.6s, target_events=[1], gamma-band 30-45Hz PLV clustering
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Directly describes methodology used to generate dataset; references conneXion study agreement 2012-A01227-36 matching dataset description.

ref_extractions.title: Dynamics of task-related electrophysiological networks: a benchmarking study
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper benchmarks source separation methods on three independent MEG datasets (button press, HCP motor tasks). While it covers task-related electrophysiology, it uses MEG data from different paradigms (motor, working memory) not the EEG visual naming dataset.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Uses MEG datasets for motor/memory tasks; no connection to EEG picture naming dataset.

ref_extractions.title: Effect of channel density, inverse solutions and connectivity measures on EEG resting-state networks reconstruction: A simulation study
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This is a simulation study using neural mass models to simulate DMN and DAN networks. It does not use real EEG data from the picture naming paradigm; purely methodological validation with simulated data.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Simulation study only; no real dataset from visual naming task used.

ref_extractions.title: Decreased integration of EEG source-space networks in disorders of consciousness
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper studies EEG functional networks in 82 subjects with disorders of consciousness (DOC patients). Different clinical population and resting-state paradigm from the healthy subjects performing visual naming in openneuro_ds003420.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Clinical study of DOC patients; different paradigm and population from picture naming dataset.

ref_extractions.title: HD-EEG for tracking sub-second brain dynamics during cognitive tasks
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This is the primary data descriptor paper for openneuro_ds003420. It describes the complete HD-EEG dataset (N=43 across two datasets) including Dataset 1 with 23 subjects performing visual naming/spelling tasks, recorded with 256-channel EGI system at 1kHz. Explicitly states data available from openneuro.org and references the conneXion study.
ref_extractions.epoch_params: tmin=0s or -0.2s, tmax varies by analysis
ref_extractions.label_mapping: Event 0=stimulus condition 0, Event 1=stimulus condition 1 (or naming trigger)
ref_extractions.super_meta_note: Reaction time stored in misc as super-level label
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Official data descriptor for exactly this dataset; describes BIDS format, experimental design, 148 pictures (74 animals, 74 tools), 23 subjects for Dataset 1.

ref_extractions.title: Exploring the temporal dynamics of speech production with EEG and group ICA
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper studies speech production dynamics in 30 Spanish subjects using picture naming with group tICA. Different dataset from a different location (Spain vs France); methodology and population do not match openneuro_ds003420.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Different subject population (Spanish speakers); no reference to conneXion study or openneuro dataset.

ref_extractions.title: Dynamic reshaping of functional brain networks during visual object recognition
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: Paper uses 20 subjects with dense 256-channel EEG during naming of meaningful (tools/animals) and meaningless (scrambled) images. Uses EEG source connectivity and modularity analysis - same research group methodology. References Braingraph study (2014-A01461-46) - a different ethics agreement from conneXion, suggesting different/extended dataset.
ref_extractions.epoch_params: tmax=0.5s post-stimulus to avoid articulation artifacts
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Same research group, similar paradigm but different ethics approval (Braingraph vs conneXion); likely Dataset 2 from same overall project but different cohort/condition.

ref_extractions.title: Microstate functional connectivity in EEG cognitive tasks revealed by a multivariate Gaussian hidden Markov model with phase locking value
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: Paper applies MGHMM method to publicly available EEG data from visual cognitive tasks but does not explicitly name the dataset. Mentions using similar methodology (PLV, K-means) to prior studies by Hassan et al. and Mheich et al. Could potentially use data from the conneXion project but this cannot be confirmed from available text.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: References prior work by same authors but does not explicitly cite openneuro_ds003420 or conneXion study.

ref_extractions.title: Dynamic Reorganization of the Cortical Functional Brain Network in Affective Processing and Cognitive Reappraisal
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper studies emotion processing and regulation using simultaneous EEG/fMRI in 20 subjects. Different experimental paradigm (emotional valence/arousal, reappraisal) from the visual naming/spelling task in openneuro_ds003420.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Different paradigm (emotion regulation); no connection to picture naming dataset.

ref_extractions.title: A NEW TECHNIQUE FOR CLASSIFICATION OF FOCAL AND NONFOCAL EEG SIGNALS USING HIGHER-ORDER SPECTRA
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper focuses on epilepsy diagnosis using focal/nonfocal EEG classification from the Bern-Barcelona database. Completely different clinical application from the cognitive visual naming paradigm of openneuro_ds003420.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Epilepsy/seizure EEG dataset; no relationship to healthy subject picture naming task.

ref_extractions.title: A Systematic Review of Aperiodic Neural Activity in Clinical Investigations
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This is a systematic review covering 177 reports across 38 clinical disorders examining aperiodic neural activity. While it discusses EEG/MEG methodology, it does not use or reference the openneuro_ds003420 dataset; it's a meta-analytic review of clinical populations.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Review article; no primary dataset used.

feasibility_reason: The dataset has well-defined event codes (0, 1) marking stimulus and response events with clear reaction time labels, and two relevant references directly support ML tasks: the cortex 2015 paper describes the 6-class brain network state segmentation methodology used to generate this dataset, and the Scientific Data paper is the official data descriptor confirming the experimental paradigm.
tasks_section:
## Tasks

### Classical Task 1: Brain Network State Segmentation in Picture Naming
- **Task Type**: classification
- **Epoch Method**: `epoch_by_event_hdf5`
- **Epoch Parameters**: tmin = -0.2 s, tmax = 0.6 s, target_events = [`trigger/D249`]
- **Label Route**: `event`
- **Meta Level**: raw
- **Target Definition**:
  | Event | y | Meaning |
  |-------|---|---------|
  | BNS1 | 0 | Brain Network State 1: 0-119ms post-stimulus |
  | BNS2 | 1 | Brain Network State 2: 120-150ms post-stimulus |
  | BNS3 | 2 | Brain Network State 3: 151-190ms post-stimulus |
  | BNS4 | 3 | Brain Network State 4: 191-320ms post-stimulus |
  | BNS5 | 4 | Brain Network State 5: 321-480ms post-stimulus |
  | BNS6 | 5 | Brain Network State 6: 481-535ms post-stimulus |
- **Evidence**:
  - DOI: 10.1016/j.cortex.2015.08.019 — Dense 256-channel EEG picture naming task identifies six brain network states (BNSs) through gamma-band (30-45Hz) phase synchronization clustering from -200ms baseline to ~600ms post-stimulus
- **Kernel Notes**: Segment epochs into 6 temporal classes based on post-stimulus latency windows. Use k-means clustering on gamma-band (30-45Hz) source connectivity features to assign BNS labels. Verify trigger/D249 corresponds to stimulus onset marker in events.tsv before epoching.

### Classical Task 2: Reaction Time Regression in Visual Object Naming
- **Task Type**: regression
- **Epoch Method**: `epoch_by_event_hdf5`
- **Epoch Parameters**: tmin = 0 s, tmax = 0.5 s, target_events = [`trigger/D249`]
- **Label Route**: `misc`
- **Meta Level**: super
- **Target Definition**:
  | Event | y | Meaning |
  |-------|---|---------|
  | `trigger/D249` | continuous | Reaction time / voice onset time (ms) from stimulus onset to vocalization |
- **Super Meta Notes**: Derived from speech recording analysis (Praat software). Kernel must extract audio onset time from the recorded oral responses and compute: y = voice_onset_time - stimulus_onset_time. Only available for subjects with valid speech responses (meaningful picture trials).
- **Evidence**:
  - DOI: 10.1088/1741-2552.aad7b1 — 256-channel EEG visual object naming correlates gamma-band (30-45Hz) network modularity metrics with reaction time (voice onset latency) from stimulus onset to 500ms
- **Kernel Notes**: Extract reaction time from misc channel or derive from audio recordings. Compute correlation between gamma-band network features and reaction time. Handle missing RT values for subjects without vocal responses (trigger/D250 meaningless picture trials excluded). Verify trigger/D249 semantic meaning in events.tsv.

### Classical Task 3: Meaningful vs Meaningless Picture Classification
- **Task Type**: classification
- **Epoch Method**: `epoch_by_event_hdf5`
- **Epoch Parameters**: tmin = 0 s, tmax = 0.5 s, target_events = [`trigger/D249`, `trigger/D250`]
- **Label Route**: `event`
- **Meta Level**: raw
- **Target Definition**:
  | Event | y | Meaning |
  |-------|---|---------|
  | `trigger/D249` | 0 | Meaningful picture stimulus (naming response expected) |
  | `trigger/D250` | 1 | Meaningless picture stimulus (silent response) |
- **Evidence**:
  - DOI: 10.1088/1741-2552.aad7b1 — Two-class visual object recognition task comparing meaningful vs meaningless images with reaction time regression; stimulus codes distinguish condition types
- **Kernel Notes**: Classify epochs based on stimulus condition. Meaningful pictures (trigger/D249) elicit vocal responses (reaction time available); meaningless pictures (trigger/D250) elicit no vocal response (participants silent). Critical: verify trigger/D249 and trigger/D250 condition mapping in events.tsv since analysis.md documented generic IDs 0/1 that do not match actual event nomenclature. Use events.tsv semantic decoding to confirm which trigger corresponds to meaningful vs meaningless conditions.
